description: Historical baseline of optical probing limits — manually curated. DREAM's qualitative claim is that the kernel's resolution λ_q is a structural cutoff (the 'pixel is real') that no engineering improvement can push lower. DREAM does NOT predict a specific value for λ_q — it is treated as a measured constant of our kernel slice (axiom A4), not a derived one. The tracker's job: watch whether the published resolution curve flattens (saturates) anywhere — if it does, that's the pixel; if it doesn't, no structural floor exists.

baseline_records.source: Abbe, E. (1873) Beiträge zur Theorie des Mikroskops
Pohl et al. (1984) — first NSOM demonstrations
Betzig et al., Rust et al. (2006) — Nobel 2014
LIGO O4 sensitivity ~10^-19 m / sqrt(Hz), 10^-14 m cumulative

dream_prediction.claim: λ_q is a structural cutoff of the projection kernel — no engineering improvement can push it lower. The pixel is real.
dream_prediction.no_specific_value: DREAM does NOT predict a numerical value for λ_q. λ_q is treated as a measured constant of our kernel slice (axiom A4), not a derived one. Any specific number quoted elsewhere as 'the kernel pixel' was illustrative, not a prediction.
dream_prediction.falsifiable_prediction: The published resolution curve flattens (saturates) at SOME scale. If the curve keeps dropping with engineering improvements indefinitely → standard physics wins, no structural floor exists, DREAM falsified. If the curve flattens anywhere → DREAM supported; the flattening scale IS λ_q.
dream_prediction.standard_physics_prediction: Resolution curve keeps dropping with engineering improvements — no structural floor.
dream_prediction.current_status: Untested — daily scout tracks new published limits to detect whether saturation occurs
